source.title: KV Compression Cannot Double as a Jailbreak Defense: The Harmfulness-then-Refusal Trajectory Guides Token Deletion
source.citation: KV Compression Cannot Double as a Jai…

record.file_problem: None; full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study constructs difference-in-means directions and applies directional interventions, including ablation and activation addition, to test their effects on refusal. It also tests whether harmfulness and refusal signals are separately represented.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s own residual-stream direction intervention and trajectory measurements, plus related key-space and attention/value patching results. Results from the paper’s proposed HaRD defense and unrelated KV-compression comparisons are not rows because they do not test the claim’s direction intervention. Values used only to select candidate layers or directions are omitted.
record.test_reason: A KV-compression defense paper, but in §3.2 it applies Arditi et al.'s two interventions, directional ablation and activation addition, to difference-in-means directions on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. It reports AdvBench refusal after residual-stream ablation (95%→29%) and refusal induction on harmless prompts (Table 7). It also reads harmfulness and refusal directions separately on four prompt groups (§4.2), which bears on V5. These results are side findings serving the defense design.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but incomplete. The main conclusion is that KV compression cannot double as a jailbreak defense: attention importance is uncorrelated with harmfulness, and key space holds no refusal-mediating direction. Harmfulness peaks at the request and refusal immediately after it. Based on this, HaRD deletes the jailbreak framing before prefill, cutting aggregate ASR from 69% to 8% and raising refusal from 30% to 88% at little utility cost. The multi-direction point appears only as a limitation citing other work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses difference-in-means directions and directional ablation/activation addition, but selects directions with a reply-inversion task and tests specified positions/layer ranges rather than the original claim’s full all-layer, all-position ablation and broad capability evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: Direction space matters: the reported key-space intervention changes AdvBench refusal from 95% to 91%, while the same data and construction in the residual stream takes it to 29%. For the selected residual refusal direction, the layer and token position are specified as layer 15 and token -2.

fits_no_version.finding: Difference-in-means directions in the key projection space barely mediate refusal. The best of 224 candidates moves AdvBench refusal from 95% to 91%, and a general contrast set leaves it at 95%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Key-projection-space difference-in-means directions do not mediate refusal, unlike the residual stream.

fits_no_version.finding: Patching attention patterns recovers 21.9% of the refusal gap and patching value vectors 68.2%; patching both recovers the full gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal information passes mainly through attention value vectors (OV) rather than attention routing (QK).

fits_no_version.finding: Layers with near-identical probe AUROC (0.998–0.999) have ablation effects ranging from +0.01 to −0.78.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear separability of harmful and harmless prompts does not identify the causal refusal direction or layer.

record.code_released: not stated (the text says an anonymous supplementary archive contains code, but gives no URL)
record.problems: The residual-direction refusal result is reported as a single rate without uncertainty in the provided text. Direction interventions and trajectory measurements are concentrated on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; the paper does not test full all-layer/all-position ablation or capability retention under that ablation. The reported transfer of HaRD to other models is not a test of direction transfer.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted candidate-direction and layer-selection values in Table 7 and Figures 3 and 17 because they are used to select directions/layers rather than reported intervention outcomes for the claim. Omitted HaRD attack-defense and utility results because those evaluate the proposed deletion method rather than the claim’s direction intervention.

untested.parts: Capability retention under ablation. Models other than Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct: Qwen and Mistral directions are used only inside HaRD, with no ablation or addition results. Ablation across all layers and positions is not specified.
No weight edit or abliterated model.

There is no measurement of jailbreaks suppressing the refusal direction (this is only cited from Hu et al.). The GCG suppression of the refusal score is an adaptive attack on HaRD, deliberately induced. There is no training against ablation.
No multi-direction, cone or affine analysis; it is mentioned only as a cited limitation.
No transfer of a direction across languages, models or stages.

missing.what: Refusal-score results by group: the refusal score crosses τr on refused harmful a median of one token after harmfulness, does not cross on accepted harmful, and does not cross on either harmless group. No row records refusal-score values or the lag.

Ablation effect versus AUROC across candidate layers and positions: ablation effects from +0.01 to −0.78 across seven layers with equal AUROC. The text is unclear whether this is residual-stream or key space.

record.verdict_notes: The record's capability_check 'y' refers to HaRD utility on LongBench and OKTest, not to capabilities under direction ablation. V1 results are side findings on one model, with no uncertainty reported. For comparison, the original reports near-complete removal on Llama-3 8B; the gap here may reflect the construction used (single position or layer, selected by reply-inversion). V5 thresholds are calibrated on the harmless groups themselves, so 'neither crosses' on those groups is partly by construction.

versions.untested_parts: The reported residual-stream ablation and addition are on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct in the specified tasks; the paper does not test every-layer, every-position ablation or general capabilities under that ablation.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration experiment.
The adaptive attack suppresses HaRD’s measured scores, not the refusal-mediating direction as a jailbreak mechanism; no training against direction ablation.
No direct multidirectional or cone intervention; the study tests a single residual-stream direction and reports residual refusal after its removal.
Tests token-level harmfulness and refusal trajectories on the described prompt groups; it does not exhaustively establish the encoding across models or tasks.
HaRD is configured separately for each model; transfer of a direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models is not tested.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or training stages.

tranche.reason: §3.2 applies Arditi et al.'s directional ablation and activation addition to DIM directions and measures refusal rates. Direction selection differs (reply-inversion, AnchorKV data), but method and measure match.

source_check.notes: The r1 and r2 rows use different directions. r1 uses the AnchorKV-data residual DIM direction. r2 uses HaRD's refusal direction (refused AdvBench vs accepted Alpaca/XSTest). The text says the code is released with the paper ('The code we release reproduces our evaluation'), but the pack says code: n, and no URL is given (anonymous). The ICLR reviewer-guideline footer is standard and addressed to human reviewers. The pack listed no [lN] ids, so label_id uses the version name.

statements.correction: ZaUq6r82Eu, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct: residual-stream DIM direction (AnchorKV's data and construction) ablated, AdvBench refusal 95%→29%. n, judge and layers not stated. The weak result, 95%→91%, is for the key-space direction, not the residual stream. Partial removal.
statements.problem: Lists this study's 95%→29% under 'ablation is weak or absent'. It is a 66-point drop that leaves 29% refusal, so partial (verdict limits_scope), not weak or absent. The '50–104 prompts' condition does not apply: the text gives no n.

statements.correction: ZaUq6r82Eu: residual-stream DIM ablation, AdvBench refusal 95%→29% (partial: 29% left). Direction built from AnchorKV's contrast set (intent-inverted AdvBench paraphrases). n, layer and judge not stated. Key-space direction: 95%→91%.
statements.problem: Puts ZaUq6r82Eu's 95%→29% in the 'No or weak effect' group. That is a large but incomplete drop, between the weak and near-full groups. differences_stated says nothing about how this study differs.

statements.correction: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Harm direction: last instruction token, layer 9, read over L6–13. Refusal direction: <|end_header_id|>, layer 15, read over L13–16. Mean max harm score: 0.182 refused harmful, 0.134 accepted harmful, 0.075/0.096 harmless groups (τh 0.114). Refusal crosses a median of one token after harm on refused harmful, and not at all on accepted harmful. No uncertainty is reported for these readings.
statements.problem: Frames the study as comparing last-instruction and template token positions. The study fixes those positions following Zhao et al. and reads both directions at every prompt token. Its controls, capability check and uncertainty belong to the defense evaluation, not to these readings. Author overlap cannot be checked (anonymous submission).
